summary: Staged commit lag in rolling release induces cross-variant session split for a subset of tenant traffic
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BrightLearn) reports that after a scheduled rolling release of a minor model revision (gptx-ef-1.2 -> gptx-ef-1.2-quant) on Dedicated capacity, a small percentage (~3-4%) of their user sessions were observed returning tokens from both the old and new model within the same conversational session.

Impact:
- Affected tenant: BrightLearn Inc. (dedicated pool).
- User-facing: mixed-model responses for ongoing chat sessions resulting in occasional semantic regressions and hallucinations.
- Scope: ~3-4% of active sessions in us-east-1 for the tenant during the 03/11 02:00-02:40 UTC window.
- Business impact: non-critical but customer reported degraded evaluation metrics and flagged to CS.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool).
- Region: us-east-1 (prod).
- Model traffic pattern: long-lived streaming sessions with token-level streaming.
- Release: staged rolling deploy (orchestrator v2.9.1) with incremental commit windows.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer started a rolling release to swap in gptx-ef-1.2-quant at 02:00 UTC with 10% cohort slices and 10-minute commit windows.
2) After workers in slice A upgraded, slice B remained on previous model; some sessions that were active and reconnected during slice commit were routed to upgraded workers for the next token batch.
3) A subset of edge connections carried affinity cookies but experienced connection handoff across a worker boundary during prewarm/drain sequences.
4) Result: single session saw initial tokens from gptx-ef-1.2 and subsequent tokens from gptx-ef-1.2-quant (and vice versa for a few sessions).

Observed behavior:
- Mixed outputs within session (content style and tokenization differences).
- No widespread 5xx or elevated latency; error rates within baseline.
- Affinity cookie values unchanged, but server-side binding appeared to rebind after worker drain.

Expected behavior:
- Sessions should maintain model-version affinity for their lifetime or be cleanly re-pinned with a documented handoff (with a new session token) to avoid mixed-model responses.

Logs & traces:
- Edge trace: edge-req-20260311-02-12-119 (shows initial handshake to worker-12, follow-up chunks to worker-19).
- Orchestrator logs: route-change events around 02:08 UTC showing staged-commit clearances with overlapping drain windows.
- Serving-runtime: KV cache miss counters spiked for the affected sessions at the exact boundary.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- We recommended aborting the in-flight rolling release and rolling back the newest cohort to restore uniform model variant across the pool.
- Suggested client-side session restart (close/reopen chat) for impacted users to re-establish consistent affinity.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: commit-stagger timing allowed edge rebinds to land on upgraded workers before session affinity token TTL was persisted to central store.
- Hypothesis 2: prewarm/drain overlap combined with connection handoff across edge proxies produced an ephemeral state where rebind logic accepted the new worker without enforcing a model-version pin check.
- Orchestrator state machine trace reveals a 90s window where cohort membership and session-lease renewal were inconsistent.
- A race identified between the binder service (edge bind cache write) and the orchestrator commit ack path. Binder wrote local affinity, but commit ack that should atomically flip model pin at the control-plane was delayed.

Action items (tracking):
- Short term: add an orchestrator guard to refuse in-flight session rebinds across differing variant labels unless session restart is performed (owner: Carlos Mendes, ETA: hotfix 2026-03-12).
- Medium term: update rolling-release runbook to increase commit quiesce window for long-lived session workloads and add pre-check to detect tokenization differences (owner: Release Eng, ETA: 2 weeks).
- Postmortem: schedule root-cause postmortem and customer debrief (owner: Lina Patel, ETA: 2026-03-19).

Resolution notes (progress):
- Mitigation: support aborted the ongoing rollout for BrightLearn at 02:18 UTC and rolled back newly upgraded workers; observed session consistency restore by 02:30 UTC.
- Hotfix: deployed route-manager guard in canary and validated on a small internal tenant; planning expedited deployment to dedicated customers with long-lived sessions.

investigation_notes:
Binder vs commit ack race: binder wrote local affinity cookie + KV cache entry before control-plane commit ack; when client reconnected mid-drain it accepted local binder state and routed to new worker despite global commit not fully synchronized. Session-lease renewal interval is 60s; commit propagation took up to 90s in observed traces under load. Edge proxy connection handoffs didn't validate model-variant label on reattach.
Repro able in lower env by simulating long-lived streaming session and forcing orchestrator commit delay >60s.
resolution: Mitigated by aborting the staged release for the customer and rolling back upgraded workers; deployed a route-manager guard that prevents session rebind across variant labels without an explicit session restart. Scheduled runbook and orchestrator fixes to enforce atomic commit semantics. Customer notified and monitoring established for next 3 rolling releases for BrightLearn.

notes: This ticket ties into broader rollout hardening work (see linked PRs). Similar races observed in historical tickets but this instance surfaced due to high percentage of long-lived streaming sessions for this tenant. Recommend prioritizing orchestration commit atomicity work across Dedicated offerings.
